differences.title: 1. TEST ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Playwright runs tests by controlling real browsers via its browser driver. It orchestrates contexts/pages and isolates sessions per test, coordinating retries and parallelism through its runner and worker model.
differences.rightDesc: Cypress executes tests inside the browser, bundling your app and runner together. Commands enqueue and later resolve, and the UI-centric runner provides live control, time travel, and consistent state visibility.

differences.title: 2. WAITING & FLakiness CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Playwright auto-waits for actionable states (visibility, stability, enabled) before interacting. It uses deterministic checks and retries internally, reducing flaky selectors without needing blanket sleeps.
differences.rightDesc: Cypress retries many assertions and commands until they pass or time out. Its execution model queues commands, so timing is governed by Cypress’ scheduler and configured default command timeouts.

differences.title: 3. BROWSER EXECUTION MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Playwright creates isolated browser contexts within a single browser process, enabling parallel tests with separate cookies/storage and configurable tracing/screenshot artifacts per context.
differences.rightDesc: Cypress drives a single browser per test run and manages app state via its own runner lifecycle. It handles cross-origin flows with dedicated configuration patterns and plugins.

differences.title: 4. NETWORK & DEVTOOLS INTEGRATION
differences.leftDesc: Playwright offers powerful network routing: intercept requests, mock responses, and inspect headers/bodies using route handlers. This integrates tightly with page events for precise, per-test control.
differences.rightDesc: Cypress provides network stubbing and spying via its cy.intercept API, hooking into the application’s traffic. Intercepts are tied to the runner lifecycle and replayed deterministically within a test.

differences.title: 5. PARALLELIZATION GRANULARITY
differences.leftDesc: Playwright parallelizes at the test level by default using worker processes/threads. It also supports per-project matrices (browser/device) so CI can scale across many combinations efficiently.
differences.rightDesc: Cypress typically parallelizes by spec files, distributing specs across machines in the Cypress Dashboard. Scaling often depends on spec partitioning and dashboard orchestration.

differences.title: 6. DEBUGGING & INSPECTION
differences.leftDesc: Playwright can record traces (actions, snapshots, network) and export them to its trace viewer. You can scrub through steps to pinpoint why selectors/actions diverged across runs.
differences.rightDesc: Cypress captures video, screenshots, and a rerunnable command log. Time travel lets you replay step-by-step states within the browser, accelerating debugging of UI regressions.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM & CI WORKFLOWS
differences.leftDesc: Playwright’s ecosystem emphasizes cross-browser automation with first-class support for CI artifacts (screenshots, traces) and robust test project configuration, working well with typical Node/Java/Python stacks.
differences.rightDesc: Cypress centers around the Dashboard for parallelization, recording, and reporting. CI integration is tightly coupled to its test runner behavior, artifacts, and dashboard project settings.
